At ~7 citations in about a month, the pace reflects a crowded, fast-moving subfield rather than a singular result—the reference list itself is dominated by 2025–2026 quantum-information-at-colliders papers, many by overlapping author groups. The appeal here is a concrete, data-ready proposal in a new channel (photons) with a clean qubit reduction that the authors note extends to h→γγ and other spin-1 systems.

arXiv:2606.26832 — Precision luminosity measurement in proton-proton collisions at √s = 13 TeV with the CMS detector (Arzunik Gevorgyan et al.)

This is CMS’s legacy Run 2 luminosity measurement, delivering 0.73% precision on the full 2015–2018 pp data set (140.22 ± 1.02 fb⁻¹)—described as the most precise ever at a bunched-beam hadron collider. The paper details the van der Meer calibration machinery and a battery of new refinements: residual orbit-drift corrections from BPM data, a two-step tracker-to-nominal length-scale calibration, an improved luminous-region treatment of transverse nonfactorization, better beam-beam modeling, and combination of four independently calibrated luminometers (HFET, HFOC, PLT, PCC). Long-term stability is validated against the Z→μμ rate, with the extracted σ_fid = 708 ± 12 pb consistent with theory.

The citation logic here is structural, not provocative: luminosity is the normalization for every cross section and, as the paper itself notes, the dominant systematic in several CMS measurements. At ~5 citations in six weeks, it is on track to become the standard reference that Run 2 CMS analyses cite for their luminosity uncertainty—the number everyone downstream simply has to quote. Its sub-percent milestone also sets the baseline going into HL-LHC.

item.title: Thursday, August 20, 2026
item.description:
Deconfinement in oxygen, and CMS at large

No single anomaly anchors the day, but CMS supplies its spine — three papers ranging from heavy ions to EFT to trigger performance. The cleanest result is the first observation of baryon-to-meson enhancement in oxygen-oxygen collisions (arXiv:2608.18256), the Λ/K⁰_S ratio showing the coalescence/radial-flow signature of a deconfined medium in a genuinely small system — the payoff the season’s OO and small-system flow program (EPOS4 scaling, ALICE ultra-central) has been building toward. Around it sit two takes on LHC Higgs-sector excesses, a collider quantum-information program that has moved past entanglement into “magic,” and a scatter of new dark-matter detection concepts.

Themes

CMS on multiple fronts

Beyond the OO result arXiv:2608.18256, CMS reports the most stringent aTGC/EFT bounds to date from WW/WZ single-lepton production with merged-jet reconstruction (arXiv:2608.18245) — another entry in the season’s steady drift toward EFT as the default language for diboson searches — and documents deep-learning heavy-flavour jet identification in the high-level trigger (arXiv:2608.18331), the unglamorous infrastructure behind the HH→4b and VBF/tt̅ H programs.

Two roads to an LHC excess

Dobrescu et al. arXiv:2608.18506 show a 10-GeV-scale ALP with h⁰→A_hA_h→(gg)(γγ) can reproduce the 3.5σ CMS diphoton excess near 13.6 GeV, with a 4g companion mode giving wide two-prong jets. Separately, Uttayarat et al. arXiv:2608.18738 propose Hγ, Hj, Hjj channels to distinguish mixing from leptophilic production behind the 146-GeV eμ excess. Two excesses, two concrete follow-up strategies — worth flagging together as the kind of loose corners current data can’t yet close.

Quantum information beyond entanglement

The collider-QI thread the memory has tracked all season takes two fresh turns. Li et al. arXiv:2608.19095 study “quantum magic” (nonstabilizerness) in QED and electroweak scattering, finding — as in earlier lab-basis work — that the physical weak mixing angle sits near the value minimizing magic production, and now tracking how the helicity basis changes the count. Yamagishi arXiv:2608.18732 argues genuine tripartite entanglement uniquely selects gauge- and diffeomorphism-invariant theories where bipartite measures were ambiguous — an extension of the entanglement-selects-symmetry line to three particles.

New handles for dark matter

Three distinct detector ideas. Matas et al. arXiv:2608.18204 give the first ab-initio calculation of DM-electron scattering in quantum dots, proposing an array of tuned morphologies whose relative rates form a “barcode” discriminating interaction operators — a genuinely new method. Scopel arXiv:2608.18609 argues JUNO’s mass plus annual modulation can reach world-leading sub-GeV spin-dependent sensitivity via the Migdal effect, and Kyriazis et al. arXiv:2608.18200 turn X-ray binary disk heating into an axion-electron probe competitive with XENONnT.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.18256 — CMS’s first observation of baryon-to-meson enhancement in OO; deconfinement signatures in a small system, the season’s OO program paying off.
  • arXiv:2608.18245 — CMS’s most stringent aTGC bounds to date from merged-jet WW/WZ; EFT as the standard diboson language.
  • arXiv:2608.18506 — Dobrescu et al. fit the CMS 13.6-GeV diphoton excess with a 10-GeV ALP from Higgs decays; a clean, testable story.
  • arXiv:2608.19095 — Quantum magic in electroweak scattering, with the weak mixing angle again near a magic-minimizing value; QI moving past entanglement.
  • arXiv:2608.18204 — Quantum-dot “barcodes” for DM-electron scattering; a novel, industrially-scalable target concept with operator-discrimination power.

From the community

The AICE proto-collaboration (57 institutions) posts a technical proposal for a ~100 m vertical atom interferometer in an LHC access shaft (arXiv:2608.18743), targeting ultralight DM and mid-band GWs — a mature, showstopper-free site pitched for LS3. On the tooling side, Kreczko’s FAST-HEP/Flow (arXiv:2608.18745) applies compiler techniques to declarative analysis workflows for long-term reproducibility.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.18920 Unified spectroscopy of P-wave flavor-sextet heavy baryons — Zhang et al. (hep-ph) — QCD sum rules tying the new Ξ_c(2882)⁰ into a coherent Ξ_c/Ω_c multiplet, with bottom-sector predictions.
  • arXiv:2608.18281 CosmoPyro: Gradients for GW Cosmology — Leyde et al. (astro-ph.CO) — differentiable hierarchical H_0 inference from GWTC-5 with Gaussian-process mass distributions; the autodiff-tooling wave reaching GW cosmology.
  • arXiv:2608.19019 Quantifying uncertainty in the neutron-star EoS — Gonçalves da Silva et al. (astro-ph.HE) — point-estimate MLPs understate high-density uncertainty; a caution that pairs with yesterday’s diffusion-model EoS.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.18256 — Observation of enhanced baryon production using strange hadrons in oxygen-oxygen collisions (CMS Collaboration)

CMS measured p_T-differential K⁰_S and Λ cross sections in OO and pp collisions at √(s_NN)=5.36 TeV (6.8 nb⁻¹ and 1.06 pb⁻¹), reconstructing the neutral strange hadrons via displaced two-track vertices. The nuclear modification factor R_OO for K⁰_S tracks that of inclusive charged hadrons, but Λ baryons are enhanced over both in the intermediate range 2<p_T<8 GeV; above 10 GeV all three converge and sit well below unity, consistent with nPDF effects plus parton energy loss. The headline is the Λ/K⁰_S cross-section ratio, which shows a pronounced enhancement in OO versus pp for 2.3<p_T<5.2 GeV, with a significance of 5.0–6.3σ across bins after accounting for correlated systematics. The ratio’s peak also shifts from p_T≈2.3 GeV in pp to ≈2.8 GeV in OO.

This is the first observation of a baryon-to-meson enhancement in OO — the quark-coalescence/radial-flow signature of a deconfined medium — in a genuinely small system, without the event-activity selections that complicate high-multiplicity pp/pPb interpretations. It caps the season’s OO program (CMS charged-hadron suppression, ALICE/ATLAS flow, Υ suppression) with a clean coalescence handle. The qualitative trends mirror PbPb and AuAu, though “less pronounced in the smaller OO system.” Caveats are honest: the Λ feed-down correction (∼18% at 5 GeV) relies on scaling ALICE Ξ/Ω ratios to the OO multiplicity, and the pp comparison inherits pileup and secondary-track corrections.

arXiv:2608.18245 — Search for anomalous couplings in WW and WZ production with single-lepton final states at √s = 13 TeV (CMS Collaboration)

Using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹), CMS searched for dimension-six EFT effects in boosted WV (WW/WZ) production where one W decays leptonically and the hadronic boson merges into a single large-R jet, tagged with mass-decorrelated ParticleNet (43% V-tag efficiency, ∼1% mistag). The m_WV spectrum (950–4550 GeV) is fit simultaneously with W+jets and tt̅ control regions, with the SM WV cross section floated (constrained to 0.32±0.1 times the NLO prediction — a notable tension the authors attribute to large LO-to-NLO K-factors and flag for dedicated measurement). Data are SM-consistent, and the analysis is statistics-limited.

The payoff is the strongest constraints to date on aTGC operators: in the HISZ basis the observed 95% intervals are c_WWW/Λ²∈[-0.93,0.93], c_W̃ WW∈[-0.37,0.49] TeV⁻², improving 30–70% over the previous 36 fb⁻¹ result. In SMEFT, c_W and c_W̃ reach [-0.08,0.08] TeV⁻² — the tightest triple-gauge bounds available — while the light-quark operators are competitive with, but not surpassing, inclusive-jet limits. This entrenches EFT with merged-jet substructure as the default diboson language, matching the digest’s theme. The main limitation is statistical, plus the approximate treatment of SMEFT operators potentially affecting background shapes (exact only in the HISZ triple-gauge case), and strong c_qq⁽³,1)–c_qq⁽³,8) degeneracy from insensitivity to color flow.

arXiv:2608.18506 — Axion-like particle at the 10 GeV scale: Higgs decays to wide jets and photons (Bogdan A. Dobrescu et al.)

Dobrescu and Roy build a renormalizable model where an ALP A_h couples to the SM only through the Higgs portal (-μ_Hϕ2v_ϕH^†H A_h A_h), with TeV-scale charge-2/3 colored scalars generating loop-induced A_h→gg (BR ∼99%) and A_h→γγ (BR ∼0.15%, fixed by 8α²/9α_s²). An effective portal coupling μ_Hϕ/v_ϕ≈10⁻² yields B(h⁰→A_hA_h)≈10%, below current undetected-width limits (<12% from ATLAS under |κ_V|≤1). The key claim: h⁰→A_hA_h→(gg)(γγ) produces an automatically boosted diphoton at M_A≈13.6 GeV that satisfies existing low-mass diphoton selections. Delphes-level cutflows give acceptance×efficiency of 12.7% (CMS) and 11.9% (ATLAS), and the model’s 1σ bands overlap both the CMS 3.5σ excess and the milder ATLAS ∼1.8σ at the same mass — reconciling the two, which under a singly-produced-ALP hypothesis appeared inconsistent.

If it holds, the CMS excess is not a lone diphoton resonance but a Higgs cascade with distinctive hadronic activity: the second A_h yields a wide jet J_gg with 2-prong substructure, and combining it with the diphoton reconstructs a 125-GeV peak (broad, from their simulation) — a background-suppression handle CMS/ATLAS could exploit. The companion h⁰→A_hA_h→4g mode (two wide jets, or (2+2)-prong when boosted) is unsearched. Caveats: the fit relies on order-of-magnitude kinematic estimates and simplified isolation proxies (large PTRatioMax to bypass rejection), not a full experimental reproduction, and the ALP mass formula requires tuned but “natural” cutoffs.

item.title: Wednesday, August 19, 2026
item.description:
Entanglement from gluons to gravitons

No single collaboration result anchors the day — the weight is spread across theory and phenomenology. The one thread that runs through it is the collider quantum-information program the memory has tracked all season, which surfaces three times: gluon-pair polarization correlations, three-qubit states in Bethe–Heitler scattering, and — from the gravity side — a third entry in the run of graviton-squeezing no-go arguments. The other cluster worth opening is a first phenomenological look at the quartic Higgs self-coupling via four-Higgs production. LHCb supplies the day’s clean null with a multimuon search.

Themes

Entanglement, from partons to gravitons

Yang et al. arXiv:2608.17685 compute the polarization density matrix of back-to-back gluon pairs, finding a maximally entangled Bell state in qq̅→gg at perpendicular emission (and a separable-but-nonzero gg→gg channel), extractable via the cos2ΔΦ energy-correlator modulation. Cao et al. arXiv:2608.18030 recast the familiar e+p→e+p+γ Bethe–Heitler process as a source of GHZ and W states. Meanwhile Fang et al. arXiv:2608.17015 show astrophysical graviton squeezing gets washed out at far-field detectors — global squeezing looks classically thermal locally. That is the third graviton-quantumness no-go in the memory, after Bao et al. and Miyauchi et al.; the wall keeps holding from new directions.

Higgs self-coupling and its CP structure

Papaefstathiou et al. arXiv:2608.16998 give the first HL-LHC study of quadruple-Higgs production in the eight-b-jet channel, setting simultaneous bounds on c_3 and d_4 — the quartic coupling, previously untouched by phenomenology. Two companion papers from Hernández-Juárez et al. probe CP structure in Higgs vertices: the SM one-loop CP-odd HWW form factor arXiv:2608.17106 (tiny, ∼10⁻⁵) and a forward-backward asymmetry in H→Zγ→f̅fγ arXiv:2608.17126 reaching 10⁻¹ at HL-LHC. Read alongside the ATLAS Higgs combination from 08-10, this is the coupling program pushing into the corners loose data can’t yet constrain.

Dark baryons and dense matter

A neutron-star cluster. Espriu arXiv:2608.17395 proposes Peccei-Quinn domain walls sweeping up quarks to seed primordial quark pellets as dark matter; Kalita et al. arXiv:2608.17409 track density-induced neutron→dark-baryon conversion in hyperon/Δ-admixed stars, with the pulsar-mass constraint disfavoring lighter χ. Panteleeva et al. arXiv:2608.17457 reconstruct the EoS with a denoising diffusion model that keeps prior, physics, and data separate — a clean template for ill-posed inverse problems. Blaschke et al. arXiv:2608.18038 add thermal twin stars as a supernova-explodability criterion.

Quantum simulation of gauge theory

Draper arXiv:2608.17115 gives an efficient block encoding of the plaquette operator in the irrep basis, removing a longstanding matrix-element scaling wall — a concrete advance for lattice-QCD quantum simulation. Hayashi et al. arXiv:2510.15493 argue for deconfinement-Higgs continuity in the SU(2) adjoint Higgs model.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.16998 — First HL-LHC phenomenology of the quartic Higgs self-coupling via four-Higgs production; opens territory single- and double-Higgs rates can’t reach.
  • arXiv:2608.17685 — Gluon pairs as a maximally entangled Bell state, read off from the energy-correlator azimuthal modulation.
  • arXiv:2608.17015 — Astrophysical graviton squeezing hidden in the far-field; the third quantum-gravity no-go in a month.
  • arXiv:2608.17457 — Diffusion-model EoS reconstruction that separates prior, physics, and data — future data reweight the posterior without retraining.
  • arXiv:2608.17855 — LHCb’s search for B→ four/six muons; a clean null with limits down to 6×10⁻¹⁰.

From the community

Grosso et al. arXiv:2608.17724 VERaiPHY — Validation & Evaluation for Robust AI in PHYsics — (hep-ph) opens a PHYSTAT series on statistical standards for ML in physics, a natural continuation of the season’s ML-methodology reckoning (the Living Guide, “Unknown Unknowns”). And Drees arXiv:2608.17864 Resolved Photon Processes: A Tribute to Rohini Godbole — (hep-ph) reviews resolved-photon physics in her memory.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.17676 Precise Measurement of δ at LBNE Using Only The Neutrino Sector — Ciuffoli (hep-ph) — trades the antineutrino sector for energy-dependence plus tight external priors on the other mixing parameters.
  • arXiv:2608.17681 An axion constraint from the diffuse supernova neutrino background — Mori et al. (hep-ph) — |g_ap|<1.3×10⁻⁹ from the recent Super-K DSNB hint, rivaling the SN 1987A bound without relying on a single event.
  • arXiv:2608.17491 An Exact Analytical Bridge from Complex Yukawa Couplings to Fermion Masses and CKM/PMNS Mixing — Lin (hep-ph) — a commutation hypothesis reducing the mass matrix to a closed-form diagonalization.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.16998 — Quadruple-Higgs boson production at the high-luminosity LHC (Andreas Papaefstathiou et al.)

First phenomenological study of gg→hhhh as a probe of the Higgs self-couplings, targeting the eight-b-jet final state at √(s)=14 TeV, 3000 fb⁻¹. The SM LO rate is tiny — σ(gg→hhhh)≃1.24×10⁻⁴ fb, a factor ∼350 below triple-Higgs — but the four-Higgs amplitude carries more quartic-coupling structure. An XGBoost classifier trained on 52 reconstructed observables, combined with a five-bin Poisson likelihood over the (c_3,d_4) plane (where c_3=κ_3-1, d_4=κ_4-1), yields simultaneous 95% bounds -10.3<c_3<11.2 and -222<d_4<234. The signal hypothesis actually combines hhhh, hhh+bb̅, and hh+4b; at the SM point it expects only 0.39 signal vs 21.9 background events. They also show hhhh→8b events with ≥6 tags feed the ATLAS hhh→6b region — with ∼89.5% tag probability the four-Higgs contribution can reach 10–100% of the hhh rate in parts of the plane.

Why it matters: the quartic coupling κ_4 is essentially unconstrained by phenomenology; this opens a channel and argues for jointly treating hhh and hhhh in inclusive multi-b analyses, complementing the ATLAS Higgs-combination push into loose corners. Caveats are heavy and honest: statistics-only limits, no detector/PDF/scale systematics, the hh+4b piece computed in m_t→∞ with only c_3 dependence, forced-splitting approximations, and sub-unit expected counts making asymptotic contours approximate. On a like-for-like basis the reach is comparable to ATLAS hhh in c_3 but weaker in d_4.

arXiv:2608.17685 — Entanglement of back-to-back gluon pair (Lei Yang et al.)

Full polarization density matrices for back-to-back gluon pairs in unpolarized pp collisions, computed at tree level for the qq̅→gg and gg→gg channels. For qq̅→gg, chirality conservation plus the MHV structure restrict the state to the |Ψ^±⟩ Bell sector; at perpendicular emission (θ=π/2) the pair becomes the pure Bell state |Ψ⁻⟩ — maximally entangled, concurrence 𝒞=-c_q(θ) reaching unity and S_max>2 (CHSH-violating) across 0<θ<π. In contrast, gg→gg is separable at all angles (𝒞=0, S_max≤10√(2)/9<2) but retains an appreciable linear-polarization correlation, c_g(π/2)=1/9≈11%. The observable link is the four-point energy correlator (E4C): contracting the pair density matrix with collinear splitting kernels maps the correlation onto a cos2ΔΦ azimuthal modulation between the two branching planes, with asymmetry 𝒜^κ=12(C_xx’+C_yy’)a^κ(n).

Why it matters: it extends the collider quantum-information program into the gluon sector, showing entanglement is generated purely by QCD helicity structure rather than a color-singlet vertex as in H→gg. The distinction between an entangled qq̅-initiated state and a merely correlated gg-initiated one is physically sharp. Caveat: the inclusive E4C signal suffers strong cancellations among qq̅ qq̅, qq̅ gg, gggg splitting channels; heavy-flavor tagging in both jets is needed to isolate QQ̅ QQ̅ and recover sensitivity. Extraction relies on the one-step collinear-splitting approximation, and the tagged sample is expected to be gg→gg-dominated with qq̅→gg as irreducible Born contamination.

arXiv:2608.17015 — Astrophysical Graviton Squeezing Can Be Hidden in the Far-Field (Cheng-Jun Fang et al.)

Using spatial quantum-optics methods extended to gravity, the authors compute the second-order coherence g⁽²⁾ accessible to a single far-field detector for gravitons emitted in a macroscopically squeezed state from a localized astrophysical source. An EFT description of squeezed-graviton generation yields Bogoliubov coefficients that inherit the source’s momentum envelope; the far-field projection (retarded pole extraction, angular stationary phase) shows a local observer effectively measures the asymptotic out-state along a single line of sight. The key result is a “same-cone” kinematic conflict: for a non-relativistic source the squeezing matrix peaks on the anti-diagonal (𝐩+𝐪≈0, back-to-back pairs), so the anomalous coherence M_D requires one internal momentum simultaneously near 𝐩 and -𝐩’ — incompatible for same-direction detection. The result is g⁽²⁾⁻²∼𝒪[exp(-2d ℰ/k_*)]+𝒪(L_D/r), so a globally squeezed state appears classically thermal (g⁽²⁾⁼²) locally.

Why it matters: this is the third graviton-quantumness no-go the memory has tracked (after Bao et al. and Miyauchi et al.), attacking macroscopic squeezing from the far-field-observability angle rather than production. Global squeezing does not guarantee local detectability. The authors frame it as a conditional no-go requiring three conditions: non-relativistic source, single localized detector, near-flat propagation. Each suggests an escape: relativistic/collinear sources (BH binaries, jets) could restore ℰ/k_*∼1; multi-detector networks probing both partner cones recover cross-correlations (feasible for a nearby solar axion halo); and strong-curvature lensing near compact objects can redirect back-to-back pairs into one cone. A concurrent independent preprint (ref. 51) reached consistent conclusions via a different framework.

item.title: Tuesday, August 18, 2026
item.description:
An old dataset, a new observable

The most distinctive work today is a three-paper package from Zhang et al. proposing and measuring the one-point charge correlator — a jet-free reformulation of the electroweak forward-backward asymmetry — extracted from archival DELPHI LEP-1 open data (arXiv:2608.14779, arXiv:2608.15357, arXiv:2608.15367). Around it sits a heavy hadron-spectroscopy load, from a lattice continuum-limit exotic-B_s result to Dudek’s review of gluonic excitations, and the usual dark-matter/axion spread. The day’s wild card is Gharibyan et al. arXiv:2608.14703, claiming evidence for parity violation in gravitational fields from HERA Compton-polarimeter spectra — an extraordinary claim that will draw extraordinary scrutiny.

Themes

A new electroweak observable from LEP open data

Zhang et al. formulate the charge flux of hadronic Z decays as a parity-odd sin(2θ) modulation measured directly against the beam axis, with no jet charge or reconstructed quark direction (arXiv:2608.14779 the theory Letter, arXiv:2608.15357 the first measurement, arXiv:2608.15367 the analysis note). The measurement, from just 61 pb⁻¹ of DELPHI data, agrees with PYTHIA and is pitched explicitly at the longstanding hadronic-asymmetry tensions. Nothing in recent memory anticipated this — it’s a genuinely new handle on precision EW, and the archival-data route is itself the point.

Hadron spectroscopy, from lattice to gluonic excitations

A dense cluster. Hudspith et al. arXiv:2608.15377 show the B_s0^* and B_s1 stay deeply bound in the continuum limit with a nonperturbatively-tuned heavy-quark action; Dudek arXiv:2608.16784 reviews glueballs and hybrids, complemented by Huang et al.’s constituent-gluon-model charmonium hybrids arXiv:2608.16250. Zhang et al. arXiv:2608.16875 ask whether the radial quarkonium ladder truncates, locating operational upper limits at n≈8–10 (cc̅). Dong et al. arXiv:2608.16266 tie X(3872) isospin breaking to a nearby partner pole. BESIII contributes throughout — the Σ⁰→Λe⁺e⁻ Dalitz decay arXiv:2608.16076, ψ(2S)→pp̅ phase arXiv:2608.15074, and new Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η modes arXiv:2608.16214.

Dark matter and axion searches

XENONnT arXiv:2608.15149 reports a null for magnetic and spin-independent inelastic DM using novel directional/kinematic selections on the recoil-plus-delayed-photon topology. Feng et al. arXiv:2608.15699 argue xenon experiments can beat Borexino on monochromatic 5.49 MeV solar axions via e⁺e⁻ pair production. Rounding out: IndIGO-D deci-Hz ultralight-DM projections arXiv:2608.15240, an ALP mono-photon channel at a muon collider arXiv:2608.15656, and a dark-charge-conjugation analysis of rare D⁰ decays arXiv:2608.15275.

QCD precision and methods

Generet et al. arXiv:2608.14793 propose projected energy correlators on the recoil against a Z/γ as a jet-algorithm-free precision-QCD benchmark, with the first NLO+NNLL matched LHC predictions. Boughezal et al. arXiv:2608.15898 establish calculable kinematic dependence of hadronization in DIS 1-jettiness event shapes; Lange et al. arXiv:2608.16744 present two-loop tensor reduction for OpenLoops.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.15357 — First measurement of the one-point charge correlator (with theory in arXiv:2608.14779); a new, jet-free EW precision observable from LEP open data.
  • arXiv:2608.14703 — Gharibyan et al.’s claimed evidence for gravitational parity violation from HERA polarimetry; extraordinary, and worth reading skeptically.
  • arXiv:2608.16875 — A first quantitative estimate of where the radial quarkonium ladder truncates; a sharp, testable challenge to the qq̅ picture.
  • arXiv:2608.14793 — Energy correlators in V+X as a clean precision-QCD benchmark, first NLO+NNLL LHC results.
  • arXiv:2608.15149 — XENONnT’s inelastic-DM search with novel directional cuts; a clean null across GeV–TeV.

From the community

Agarwalla et al. arXiv:2608.15231 Deep Earth imaging through neutrino and seismic tomography — Agarwalla et al. (hep-ex) — a report from the DENSITY 2026 mini-workshop bridging seismology, geochemistry, mineral physics, and neutrino physics; interdisciplinary field-building rather than a result.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.14785 Unveiling Neutrino Nature with the Diffuse Supernova Background — Manno et al. (astro-ph.HE) — DSNB as a Dirac/Majorana discriminant via resonant chirality flips, given magnetic moments ≳10⁻¹⁴μ_B.
  • arXiv:2608.14794 Radiative corrections to neutron β decay with explicit Δ(1232) — Gialidi et al. (hep-ph) — the EM axial-coupling shift halved versus the Δ-less result; relevant to lattice-vs-experiment g_A.
  • arXiv:2608.16783 Quantum Simulation of QCD in Axial Gauge — Yao (hep-lat) — polynomial qubit and gate scaling for 3+1D SU(3) with fermions by solving Gauss’s law away.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.15357 — First measurement of the one-point charge correlator in e⁺e⁻ collisions at √(s)=91.2 GeV with DELPHI Open Data (Jingyu Zhang et al.)

Zhang et al. deliver the first-ever measurement of the one-point charge correlator — the net electric-charge flux 𝒬(θ) into the detector as a function of polar angle relative to the e⁻ beam — from 61 pb⁻¹ of archival DELPHI Open Data (46 pb⁻¹ in 1994, 15 pb⁻¹ in 1995). This is a jet-free, hemisphere-free, IRC-safe reformulation of the hadronic forward-backward asymmetry: the parity-odd cosθ coupling structure shows up directly as a sin(2θ) modulation in the charge-weighted track density (tracks with p_T>2 GeV, 20°≤θ≤160°). Detector effects are handled in two stages — a PYTHIA 8.3-based correction for track-finding, fakes and charge misID, then a data-driven tag-and-probe measurement of the residual data–MC charge-misreconstruction bias in Z→τ⁺τ⁻ events, where charge conservation fixes the probe’s true sign. The fully corrected result exhibits the expected sin(2θ) shape, negative in the forward hemisphere, crossing zero at 90°, and agrees with PYTHIA 8.3 within uncertainties.

Why it matters: this establishes experimental viability of a genuinely new precision-EW handle, one whose relation to the Z couplings is not mediated by jet-charge model dependence — the very ambiguity blamed for the persistent A_FB^b tension. The construction extends to heavy-flavor currents where tensions are largest, and prefigures Tera-Z programs at FCC-ee/CEPC. The honest caveat is prominent: this is a proof-of-principle, not a competitive extraction. Systematics (27.6%/35.6% at θ=55°/125°) dominate over statistics and are set by the τ control-sample size; the parity-odd bias component is bounded, not measured to vanish. Sagitta and photon-conversion calibrations are the named next steps.

arXiv:2608.14703 — Evidence for parity violation in gravitational fields (V. Gharibyan et al.)

Gharibyan et al. analyze 314,896 Compton spectra from the HERA transverse polarimeter (2004–2007), tagged by 514.5 nm laser helicity, and report a laser-helicity-dependent asymmetry in the Compton-edge energy (ω_max=13.9 GeV) of A=(4.89±0.52)×10⁻⁵, claimed at 9σ. Within a phenomenological framework where the gravitational coupling acquires a helicity-dependent term G_s=G+(𝐬·𝐏/P)ΔG_𝒫, the modified energy-momentum relation shifts ω_max oppositely for the two helicities, and the γ² amplification factor sets the sensitivity. They translate the asymmetry into a helicity-dependent gravitational-potential difference ΔU_𝒫=(1.71±0.036±0.187)×10⁻¹⁴, i.e. ΔG_𝒫/G=(5.7±0.6)×10⁻¹⁰ using summed local potentials (dominated by the Virgo Supercluster). The signal is isotropic in right ascension (constant fit checked against 64 bins), which they argue excludes Lorentz-violating vector theories, and they estimate instrumental false asymmetries from transverse/longitudinal beam polarization and linear-light contamination to be sub-dominant.

Why it matters: if real, this would be the first high-energy test of a discrete symmetry in gravity showing violation, with speculative implications for galactic rotation curves via a chiral-gravity shift of the 21 cm line — potentially bearing on dark matter. But this is an extraordinary claim resting on a 5×10⁻⁵ edge shift in a polarimeter never built to measure absolute energy asymmetries. The authors themselves flag “hidden systematic factors”: helicity-dependent detector gain (estimated opposite-sign from bremsstrahlung fits, but uncorrected due to unknown beam offsets on an inhomogeneous calorimeter) and helicity-correlated laser spatial jitter convolved with the lepton phase space. The digest’s “read skeptically” is well-earned.

arXiv:2608.16875 — Truncation of the Radial Ladder in Heavy Quarkonia (Wen-Xuan Zhang et al.)

Zhang, Luo and Liu ask whether the radial excitation ladder of quarkonia terminates, solving a screened relativized Godfrey–Isgur Hamiltonian for cc̅ and bb̅ via the Gaussian expansion method (N_max=20, r_max=30 fm) up to n=14. Screened confinement replaces the linear term’s unbounded rise with a plateau M_∞=m_1+m_2+b/μ+c, giving limiting masses of 4.74 GeV (cc̅) and 11.67 GeV (bb̅). Crucially, while masses saturate — adjacent gaps dropping below 10 MeV — RMS radii keep diverging to ∼10–50 fm, an order of magnitude past the confinement scale. This “mass–radius decoupling” defines a breakdown of the qq̅ picture. A threshold criterion (min gap <10 MeV with radius increments >3/2 fm), corroborated by CUSUM/two-segment changepoint analysis of log(ΔR/ΔM) and a resolvability index χ_n=ΔM_n R_n collapsing below unity, locates operational upper limits at n≈8–10 for charmonium (D-waves first, then P, then S) and n≈12–13 for bottomonium. Staged χ² fits give RMS mass residuals of 34/24 MeV (10/4 MeV for low-lying states), with the charmonium screening length μ⁻¹≈1.4 fm inside the lattice string-breaking range.

Why it matters: this is the first quantitative answer to a long-standing spectroscopy question, and it is directly testable — no new charmonia should appear above ∼4.7 GeV, and BESIII/Belle II/LHCb can probe this. Caveats are candidly stated: high-n bottomonium shows round-off artifacts; the thresholds are empirical; and the truncation value is model-input-dependent (alternative fits give 4.61–4.83 GeV). Formal parameter errors are not quoted. The manuscript was substantially AI-drafted (Grok, GPT-5.4), per the authors’ declaration.

item.title: Monday, August 17, 2026
item.description:
Flavor, precision not tension

After a week where the flavor front ran on anomalies, today it runs on consolidation. LHCb posts an improved ϕ_s from B⁰_s→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ (arXiv:2608.14119), landing squarely on the SM; Huang et al. arXiv:2608.14341 supply the last missing factorization ingredient for b→sℓℓ at leading power — the theory-side counterpart to the C_9 story that peaked mid-week; and a kaon global fit (arXiv:2608.14474) folds in the new K⁺→π⁺νν̅ and LFU observables. The standout curiosity is elsewhere: Alves et al. arXiv:2608.13736 argue neutrino oscillations are not blind to absolute mass after all. A lighter day overall, weighted toward theory and tooling.

Themes

Flavor: penguins, kaons, and a clean φs

Three complementary entries. LHCb’s arXiv:2608.14119 gives ϕ_s=-0.041±0.017 rad in the full combination — precise and SM-consistent, a null against the week’s flare. Huang et al. arXiv:2608.14341 complete the twist-3 three-particle B-DA contribution to B→{K,π}ℓℓ at NLO, exactly the theory control the C_9 interpretation needs. D’Ambrosio et al. arXiv:2608.14474 show KOTO-II can discriminate the two surviving NP minima in the kaon sector, with NA62 complementary.

ML tooling meets model misspecification

Three ML papers, with a rare conceptual center. Cruz-Martinez et al. arXiv:2608.13633 is a methodology piece on “unknown unknowns” — when misspecification is the discovery and when it must be absorbed (see community). Jia et al.’s ORCA arXiv:2608.13652 attacks the interpretability problem in anomaly detection via contrastive embeddings that support template attribution; Hermansen et al.’s Pairton arXiv:2608.14278 reframes decay reconstruction as iterative masked edge prediction, SOTA on hadronic tt̅.

Vector-like fermions at future e+e-

Two independent takes on VLFs as an e⁺e⁻ target. Liu et al. arXiv:2608.14195 study single first-generation singlet-VLL production, reaching 900 GeV (ILC) to 1400 GeV (CLIC) via boosted fat-jets. Marzo et al. arXiv:2608.14538 compute one-loop VLF effects on Higgs-strahlung and find Yukawa-driven scenarios shift σ(ZH) at the per-mille FCC-ee level — mixing-driven ones already killed by EWPO. This extends the season’s FCC-ee precision thread.

Axion cosmology and strong CP

Kitajima et al. arXiv:2608.13650 show axion isocurvature from inflationary fluctuations survives domain-wall scaling and annihilation. Benincasa et al. arXiv:2608.13692 use a dim-6 PQ operator to trigger a first-order transition with observable GWs. Liu et al. arXiv:2608.13796 tie θ̅=0 and quark mass hierarchies to non-Abelian modular invariance.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.13736 — Oscillations do carry absolute-mass information at NLO in m_i/E; JUNO reaches few-hundred-keV sensitivity to a novel mass combination. A genuinely surprising conceptual point.
  • arXiv:2608.14341 — The last missing leading-power factorization piece for b→sℓℓ; the theory side of the week’s C_9 story.
  • arXiv:2608.14119 — LHCb’s improved ϕ_s in B_s→J/ψππ, precise and SM-consistent.
  • arXiv:2608.14474 — Kaon global fit showing KOTO-II can discriminate viable NP scenarios; a concrete near-term target.
  • arXiv:2608.14538 — VLF loop effects reaching per-mille Higgs-strahlung shifts; Yukawa couplings, not mixing, as the FCC-ee target.

From the community

Cruz-Martinez et al. arXiv:2608.13633 Unknown Unknowns: Model Misspecification in Machine Learning for Physics (physics.data-an) — less a technique than a disposition: robustness against being wrong in unanticipated ways, framing detection and mitigation as an iterative loop. A natural companion to this season’s ML-methodology reckoning (the Living Guide, RooAgent).

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.14268 W+charm in GM-VFNS — Alanko et al. (hep-ph) — charge-ratio observable favors zero strangeness asymmetry (CT18A) over MSHT20/NNPDF4.0 against ATLAS data.
  • arXiv:2608.14419 NNLO QCD corrections to WWγ — Garbarino et al. (hep-ph) — +16% over NLO, uncertainties down to ±4%; a quartic-gauge-coupling input.
  • arXiv:2608.13710 Optical characterization of commercial PVT scintillators — Huggins et al. (physics.ins-det) — measured n(λ) shifts photon counts 7% versus manufacturer values; a Geant4 calibration reference.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.13736 — Beyond Δm²: Absolute Mass Sensitivity in Neutrino Oscillations (Gustavo F. S. Alves et al.)

The headline is conceptual: the oscillation phase, expanded beyond leading order in mᵢ/E, contains a term ∝ (mᵢ⁴−mⱼ⁴)L/E₀³ = Δmᵢⱼ²(mᵢ²+mⱼ²)L/E₀³, so oscillations do carry absolute-mass information through the mass-squared sum. The authors show this cannot be recovered from naive plane-wave prescriptions — equal-energy, equal-momentum, and various t↔L replacements disagree at NLO — and derive it properly with a wave-packet treatment that fixes each eigenstate’s mean energy/momentum from beta-decay kinematics (an effective two-body decay N_A→(N_B e)+ν̄). The production-dependent correction enters only at the per-mille level (E₀/m_A ≲ 10⁻⁴). Applied to JUNO’s 52.5 km reactor baseline, a χ² fit to ~9.5×10⁴ IBD events over six years yields sensitivity m₁ < 305 keV (1σ), 434 keV (2σ) with oscillation parameters profiled; the solar channel dominates because its broad dip lands in JUNO’s high-statistics band and survives energy smearing intact.

Why it matters: this overturns the textbook statement that oscillations measure only Δm². It is a genuinely new, mechanism-independent absolute-mass probe, sensitive to a different combination than beta decay (m_νe), 0νββ (m_ββ), or cosmology (Σmᵢ). The honest caveat is scale: at few-hundred-keV, this is ~10⁴× weaker than KATRIN (0.45 eV) and ~10⁷× weaker than cosmology (0.053 eV), and the sensitivity is limited by a degeneracy in which the NLO shift mimics a rescaling Δm₂₁²→Δm₂₁²(1+m₁²/2E₀²), broken only by the 1/E₀² energy dependence.

arXiv:2608.14341 — Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin B-Meson Decays (Yong-Kang Huang et al.)

Using SCET with two-step QCD→SCET_I→SCET_II matching, the authors compute for the first time the subleading-twist correction to B→{K,π}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ from the three-particle twist-three B-meson distribution amplitude at NLO, plus new NNLO corrections to the spectator-scattering (C-type) and weak-annihilation topologies and the O(α_s) D-type spectator term. This is billed as the last missing ingredient for a complete leading-power factorization proof of the b→{s,d}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ matrix element. The three-particle convolution integrals over the two soft momenta are shown to converge, and the new jet function J_C^(3P) is validated by a second, method-of-regions calculation. Numerically, the newly included leading-power effects shift both real and imaginary parts of the top-sector amplitude T_π⁰ by O(30%) in q²∈[1.5, 4.0] GeV², driven by cancellation among A- and B-type pieces; the largest phenomenological impact is on the direct-CP-asymmetry differences ΔA_CP(B→Pℓℓ), shifted 15–20% at large recoil, where the nontrivial strong phase of J_C^(3P) dominates.

Why it matters: this is the theory-side counterpart to the week’s C₉ story — tightening the leading-power factorization control that any short-distance NP interpretation of b→sℓℓ requires. The honest caveat is that it does not resolve the anomaly: branching fractions for B⁰→K⁰ℓℓ and B⁺→K⁺ℓℓ “remain in sharp tension” with Belle/CDF/LHCb/CMS at large recoil, and the new B⁺→π⁺ℓℓ predictions actually favor old LHCb data over the latest full-Run-1+2 result (1.1–2.5σ).

arXiv:2608.14119 — Improved measurement of CP violation in B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ decays (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb performs a time-dependent, flavour-tagged amplitude analysis of ~94,000 B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ signal decays from the full Run 2 6 fb⁻¹ sample (38 fs decay-time resolution, 4.5% tagging power), extracting φₛ = −0.077 ± 0.034 ± 0.007 rad, |λ| = 0.993 ± 0.026 ± 0.007, and Γ_H = 0.610 ± 0.002 ± 0.004 ps⁻¹. The π⁺π⁻ spectrum is modelled with six resonances plus a nonresonant term — adding an f₂(1565) contribution to a small ~1.6 GeV peak relative to earlier work — with the CP-odd f₀(980) carrying 72.5% fit fraction. Combining with Run 1 gives φₛ = −0.046 ± 0.031 rad; folding in all other LHCb channels yields φₛ = −0.041 ± 0.017 rad (χ²/ndf = 35/30), consistent with the J/ψφ average and improving precision by ~15%.

Why it matters: against a week where the flavour front ran on anomalies, this is a clean null. The result sits squarely on the SM prediction φₛ^SM = −0.0376₋₀.₀₀₀₅⁺⁰·⁰⁰⁰⁶ rad, and no direct CP violation is seen (|λ| compatible with 1). The main caveat is explicit in the text: subleading penguin contributions are neglected throughout — externally constrained to a Δφₛ = 5.0 ± 4.6 mrad shift from B⁰→J/ψρ⁰ — and the production asymmetry A_P is fixed to zero (a ±2% variation is taken as systematic). Systematics remain subdominant to the 34 mrad statistical uncertainty on φₛ.

item.title: Friday, August 14, 2026
item.description:
LHCb’s CP-violation harvest

The day’s weight sits squarely on a trio of LHCb papers dissecting B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ on the 2011–12 dataset (arXiv:2608.12612, arXiv:2608.12613, arXiv:2608.12614) — an amplitude analysis that lands six CP-violation phenomena as significant for the first time and reorders the Kππ S-wave picture in favor of QCD factorization. This lands the day after yesterday’s twin B-anomaly flare (C_9 transversity and the B→PP SU(3) fit); the flavor front stays hot, but this is measurement, not tension. Around it, a dense cluster of weak-scale dark-matter model-building, a tomographic-CP top paper extending the season-long QI thread, and two differentiable neutrino toolkits posted the same day.

Themes

LHCb’s charmless three-body CP violation

The three companion papers share the 3 fb⁻¹ sample but split the story: arXiv:2608.12612 delivers the amplitude analysis with three independent S-wave treatments (isobar, K-matrix, quasi-model-independent) that agree; arXiv:2608.12613 resolves the long-standing K^*_0(1430) S-wave puzzle by relaxing unitarity assumptions, eliminating the ad-hoc f_X(1300); and arXiv:2608.12614 is the headline — discovery of CP violation in ρ(770)⁰K⁺, first evidence in ππ rescattering and in a spin-3 resonance, and CP violation in S–P and S–D wave interference driven by long-distance dynamics. This is the data-side counterpart to yesterday’s semileptonic and non-leptonic anomalies.

Weak-scale dark matter, revisited economically

A notable pile-up of DM model-building. Bhattiprolu et al. arXiv:2608.12480 map the singlet-doublet fermion model across freeze-out, co-scattering, freeze-in and SuperWIMP, emphasizing the small-Yukawa regime where detection goes collider-only. Borah et al. arXiv:2608.12483 reuse singlet-doublet fermions for an inverse first-order EW phase transition plus radiative Dirac neutrino mass, and Belfkir et al. arXiv:2608.12646 present a new one-loop Majorana-mass topology with viable fermionic/scalar DM. Datta et al.’s spontaneous scoto-leptogenesis arXiv:2608.12497 extends the running baryogenesis/scotogenic thread.

Tomography turned toward CP

Perelstein et al. arXiv:2608.12463 use top-pair spin tomography to build CP-sensitive observables for (chromo-)electric dipole operators, reaching 40–200 TeV scales at the LHC/HL-LHC and 10–15 TeV at FCC-ee — beating traditional observables. This is the collider-QI program the memory has tracked from tt̅ to TauPolaris, now aimed at CP violation rather than entanglement per se.

Differentiable neutrino engines

Two autodiff oscillation packages the same day: Granger’s MANGO arXiv:2608.13429, which differentiates through geometry and Earth-shell densities for tomography and experimental-design metrics, and Eller et al.’s Newtrinos.jl arXiv:2608.12940, a modular Julia global-fit framework. Both bet on gradient-based inference as the default for the next round of oscillation analyses.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.12614 — LHCb: six CP-violation phenomena in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ established at once, including the first in wave interference and in a spin-3 state. The day’s result.
  • arXiv:2608.12463 — Perelstein et al. turn spin tomography into optimal CP-dipole observables; the QI program’s CP turn, with concrete FCC-ee/LHC reach.
  • arXiv:2608.12793 — BESIII’s space-like η’ transition form factor, sub-3% below Q²⁼¹.5 GeV² and a first at Q²<0.3 — a clean input for hadronic light-by-light in g-2.
  • arXiv:2608.13429 — MANGO: fully differentiable oscillation engine that gets all 369 Earth-model gradients at the cost of six parameters.
  • arXiv:2608.12480 — A clean map of singlet-doublet DM across all production mechanisms; likely the reference for the small-Yukawa regime.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.12616 Axion-Like Particle Search with a Hybrid Cherenkov-Scintillation Detector — Aguilar-Arevalo et al. (hep-ex) — CCM beam-dump ALP search, surpassing CCM120 with less exposure via optical discrimination.
  • arXiv:2608.13525 A pion-driven near-threshold enhancement in the π T_cc system — Brandão et al. (hep-ph) — a predicted πT_cc resonance at ~4055 MeV, molecule-as-building-block, searchable in D⁰D⁰π⁺π⁻.
  • arXiv:2608.12706 Scalar induced gravitational waves as probes of dark QCD — Feng et al. (hep-ph) — a dark-confinement crossover imprints a frequency-shifted SIGW distortion.
  • arXiv:2608.12467 Soft Collinear Effective Theory for Heavy QCD Axions — Bisht et al. (hep-ph) — SCET factorization for B→Ka, quantifying when spectator scattering matters.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.12614 — Observation of several sources of CP violation in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

Working the full 3 fb⁻¹ Run 1 sample (115,102 candidates, 88.7% purity), LHCb performs an amplitude analysis of B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ with three independent treatments of the troublesome Kπ and ππ S-waves (isobar/GLASS, K-matrix, and a first-of-its-kind quasi-model-independent binning of two crossing partial waves). All three agree, and six CP-violation phenomena clear observation-level significance at once. The headline first observations: quasi-two-body CPV in B⁺→ρ(770)⁰K⁺, 𝒜_CP=+0.280±0.022±0.029 (minimum 5.9σ across S-wave models); and in B⁺→f_2(1270)K⁺, rejected at 8.2–9.1σ at amplitude level. First evidence appears for CPV in the elastic ππ-ππ rescattering S-wave below the 4π threshold (𝒜^S_CP=+0.665±0.032±0.053), in S–P interference with ρ(770) (5.4σ), in S–D interference near the f_2(1270) (≥4.4σ), and — a genuine first — in a spin-3 state, ρ_3(1690)⁰ (≥3.3σ).

Notably, no CPV is seen in ρ⁰–ω mixing, contrary to several predictions; this dilution explains why the fitted ρ(770) asymmetry exceeds the model-independent P-wave value (0.150±0.022). A large positive asymmetry immediately above ππ threshold resists all three models, hinting at sizeable cc̅-loop or isospin-2 contributions. Systematics are comparable to statistical uncertainties throughout — good model control, but a signal that Run 1 statistics can no longer fully exploit. This is the measurement-side counterpart to the season’s flavor anomalies, sharpening reference points for γ extraction and B→Kπ-type isospin sum rules.

arXiv:2608.12463 — Probing CP-violating top-quark dipole moments with tomographic observables (Maxim Perelstein et al.)

Perelstein, Shaik and Youn recast tt̅ spin tomography as a CP-violation search. Symmetry fixes which Fano coefficients a CP-odd (chromo-)electric dipole can populate: the normal polarization difference ΔB_n and the antisymmetric normal-plane correlations A_rn, A_kn, all exactly zero in the SM (three-loop suppressed). They compute the production density matrix in closed form for e⁺e⁻, qq̅ and gg, build the statistically optimal CP-odd observable O_opt=f_1/f_0 (proven to saturate the Cramér–Rao bound), and carry the analysis to Delphes detector level. Projected 95% CL reach on inverse couplings: 10–15 TeV for the electroweak electric dipoles d_γ,d_Z at FCC-ee (365 GeV, 3 ab⁻¹), and 40 (200) TeV for the top chromo-EDM at LHC Run 2 (HL-LHC) — exceeding the conventional triple/quadruple-product observables (e.g. the CMS O_1 search) used today. d_γ projects mainly onto A_rn, d_Z onto ΔB_n; the optimal weight combines them for ~40 TeV parton-level FCC-ee reach.

A sharp negative result accompanies this: they prove a no-go theorem that the top–antitop discord asymmetry Δ𝒟 (and geometric discord, steering asymmetry) vanishes identically for the dipoles, contradicting a recent claim that advertised it as a CP probe — the reported nonzero values are CP-even absorptive artifacts. Caveats: reach at FCC-ee threshold is diluted by poor top-direction reconstruction (∼40^∘, dilution factors 0.24–0.40); systematics are assumed subdominant, and the EFT-consistent linear-order truncation neglects dimension-eight-degenerate terms.

arXiv:2608.12793 — High-precision measurement of the space-like η’ transition form factor (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

BESIII measures the single-virtual space-like η’ TFF via single-tag two-photon fusion e⁺e⁻→e⁺e⁻η’ on 20.3 fb⁻¹ at 3.773 GeV, reconstructing η’→π⁺π⁻γ and π⁺π⁻η. The result spans Q²∈[0.1,6.0] GeV² in 18 fine bins, reaches better than 3% precision below 1.5 GeV², and provides the first direct determination at Q²<0.3 GeV² — filling the gap between BaBar (>4 GeV²) and L3 (<0.15 GeV², which inferred Q² indirectly from the η’ transverse momentum). Tight control of the untagged-photon virtuality (Q²_miss∈[0,0.08] GeV², with a +1.0% correction to Q²_miss=0) is the key improvement; total systematics run 2.5–4.7% on the cross section, halved on the TFF.

The extracted values are the most precise to date and lie systematically above earlier data — attributed to the larger, less-controlled Q²_miss of prior measurements. Crucially, the data agree with lattice QCD (BMW) and holographic (LMR) predictions while sitting above data-driven dispersive models. Since LQCD and holographic approaches also predict a larger a_μ^η’ than the data-driven evaluation, this input feeds directly into the hadronic light-by-light contribution to muon g-2 — where LQCD HLbL now runs ~50% above the 2020 white-paper number — and the authors flag that existing data-driven analyses may warrant re-evaluation. The result also constrains the η’ gluonic component and η’ production models.

Citation radar

This week’s radar points to the speculative frontier of flavor model-building, where a single-paper octonionic construction is drawing early attention less for a confirmed result than for staking out sharply falsifiable predictions in the neutrino sector.

arXiv:2606.27836 — Leptonic CP Conservation and the Quark CP Phase from Octonionic Flavor Structure (Bishnu Gupta Teli et al.)

Working within the octonionic unification programme — one Standard-Model generation realized on complexified octonions via the Clifford algebra 𝒞l(6), extended to three generations by G_2 automorphisms and ladder-operator rotors — Teli and Singh prove a localization theorem for where a CP-violating phase can live. Their central claims are asymmetric and clean: the quark (1,2) transport is the occupation flip of a single ladder mode, forcing A_d = A_u^* and the exact one-parameter law ϕ_12 = -2χ, with the programme’s geometric rotor sitting at the maximal, quadrature-balanced point |ϕ_12|=π/2. For leptons they prove a “reality theorem”: every charged-lepton and neutrino transport amplitude is real for the entire admissible transport class, so leptonic Dirac CP is conserved (J_ℓ=0, δ^ℓ_CP∈{0,π}) unless a Higgs “bridge” mixes the identity line with the lepton-flavor plane — the sole, uncomputed loophole. A minimality assumption on the neutrino Jordan spectrum (-δ_ν,0,+δ_ν) then selects inverted ordering, m_ββ≃19 meV and Σm_ν≃0.10 eV.

Notably, the authors themselves quantify “the lean,” conceding that current global fits disfavor their inverted-ordering-plus-conserved-CP package at roughly 3σ per axis, with DESI cosmology also in tension. The ~5 citations two months out most plausibly reflect internal traffic within this tightly-knit programme (many references are the authors’ own companion papers), amplified by the paper’s unusually explicit falsification table tied to JUNO, DUNE, Hyper-K, and next-generation 0νββ. The reason for broader uptake is not yet visible from the text; the appeal is a concrete, near-term-testable prediction rather than an established measurement. (The acknowledgments also flag heavy reliance on AI tools in the derivations.)

item.title: Thursday, August 13, 2026
item.description:
The B anomalies come back, from data

After a week of neutrino mixing numerology, the weight today swings to flavor — but from the data side, not model-building. LHCb posts a model-independent measurement of the B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ transversity amplitudes arXiv:2608.12215 with the C_9 deviation landing at 4.3–4.8σ depending on binning, and Bouchard et al. arXiv:2608.11298 find the B→PP global fit under SU(3)_F off by 4.1σ, with SU(3)-breaking parameters that make no sense in the SM. Two independent hadronic/semileptonic B anomalies in one day is the story. Around them sit a precision NOvA antineutrino–hydrogen cross section, an FCC-ee Higgs-mass study reaching the natural width, and a clean Majoron EFT.

Themes

B-physics anomalies, data-driven

The LHCb amplitude analysis arXiv:2608.12215 is the one to open: rather than fitting angular observables in fixed q² bins, they reconstruct the transversity amplitudes from Legendre polynomials, letting global fits choose their own binning and disentangling hadronic contamination from a genuine C_9 shift — which survives at 4.3–4.8σ. Bouchard et al. arXiv:2608.11298 attack from the non-leptonic side: their B→PP fit demands ~1000% SU(3)_F breaking, worsening to ~5σ under theory constraints. Different sectors, same direction. Nothing in the recent memory anticipated a data-side flare-up of this size.

Neutrino cross-sections and Majorons

NOvA arXiv:2608.12293 delivers the most precise ν̅_μH→μ⁺ⁿ CCQE cross section to date (35,509 events, systematics four times below the flux uncertainty) — directly usable to constrain the absolute antineutrino flux. That speaks straight to last week’s DUNE cross-section-systematics warning (Puhan et al.): the field is starting to pin down the very inputs that were shifting sensitivities 25–30%. On the model side, Biggio et al. arXiv:2608.11522 build a Majoron EFT from Type I/II/III seesaws with a single VEV, so invisible Higgs width, Majoron–lepton coupling and leptonic non-unitarity all become locked relations — falsifiable even if the new states sit far out of reach.

Collider precision and EFT matching

Eysermans et al. arXiv:2608.12071 show FCC-ee can reach 4 MeV Higgs-mass precision in leptonic ZH recoil — comparable to the natural width, the enabling step for resonant electron-Yukawa production. This extends the SMEFT-precision thread the memory has tracked (Haisch’s NLL EWPO, Celada’s FCC-ee accounting). Dittmaier et al. arXiv:2608.11306 give a functional one-loop matching recipe for the Higgs singlet extension, noting the emergent EFT only maps to SMEFT at the cost of fermionic operators; Deng et al. arXiv:2608.12079 resum a quasi-collinear divergence in the missing-mass spectrum of invisible dark-photon production.

Dark matter and exotic-state searches

Two NaI(Tl) hardware papers land together — temperature-dependent SiPM readout arXiv:2608.11303 and the COSINE-100U encapsulation upgrade arXiv:2608.11678, both chasing lower thresholds for low-mass DM. LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA arXiv:2608.11620 excludes ultralight scalar/vector bosons via black-hole superradiance, and a mirror-neutron search arXiv:2608.12173 sets the first lab limit on peV-scale n–n’ splitting that beats the neutron-star-cooling bound.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.12215 — LHCb’s model-independent C_9 from transversity amplitudes, 4.3–4.8σ and binning-flexible; the flavor result of the day.
  • arXiv:2608.11298 — Bouchard et al.’s B→PP fit demanding absurd SU(3)_F breaking; a second, independent B-anomaly hint.
  • arXiv:2608.12293 — NOvA’s most-precise ν̅_μ–H CCQE cross section, poised to constrain absolute flux.
  • arXiv:2608.11522 — Biggio et al.’s Majoron EFT: seesaw scale falsified through locked relations, not direct production.
  • arXiv:2608.12071 — FCC-ee reaching 4 MeV Higgs-mass precision, the gateway to the electron Yukawa.

From the community

Xiao et al. arXiv:2608.11712 Physics of the Electron-Ion Collider in China — Bo-Wen Xiao et al. (hep-ph) lays out the EicC physics case, deliberately foregrounding newer directions — nucleon mass decomposition, energy-energy correlators, quantum information, ML — over the well-reviewed 3D-structure staples.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.11316 Particle Production, Equilibration, and Quantum Recurrences from Classical Fields — Cuntín et al. (hep-ph) — lattice λϕ⁴ as a quantum-computable route to non-equilibrium QFT, with Poincaré recurrences after equilibration.
  • arXiv:2608.11467 First polarized SDMEs in ω photoproduction — Hu et al. (nucl-ex) — CLAS pushes into the Regge regime, first measurements for -t>0.6 GeV².

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.12215 — Model-independent measurement of the transversity amplitudes of the B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ decay (LHCb collaboration et al.)

LHCb reconstructs the full set of B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ transversity amplitudes unbinned in q² over 1.1<q²<8.0 GeV²/c⁴, expanding each P-wave amplitude in four Legendre polynomials (32 parameters, S-wave as nuisance) fitted to 8.4 fb⁻¹. The orthogonality of the Legendre basis reduces amplitude correlations relative to earlier empirical parametrisations, and CP-averaged observables (S_5, A_FB, etc.) are then built as continuous functions of q². Systematics run 0.09–0.35 of the statistical error, dominated by kinematic/trigger corrections. Profiling in flavio with the Ref. [14] baseline binning gives Re(C_9^NP)=-1.17⁺⁰.21_-0.20, a 4.3σ pull; quartering the bins tightens to -1.17⁺⁰.19_-0.18 and 4.8σ.

The key point is methodological: because hadronic (long-distance) contributions and a genuine NP C_9 shift have distinct q² dependences, the unbinned amplitude reconstruction lets global fits choose their own binning and, in principle, disentangle the two. The C_9 deviation surviving this more flexible treatment — and growing with finer q² resolution — is exactly what one expects from a real short-distance effect rather than a mismodelled charm-loop contamination. Results agree with the latest binned angular analysis [14]. Caveat: the interpretation still fixes all other Wilson coefficients to SM values and imports SM hadronic nuisance parameters through flavio’s covariance; the significance is a one-parameter statement, and the amplitude fit assumes no scalar/timelike contributions and a uniform-in-q² S-wave. The disentangling of hadronic versus NP awaits improved theory predictions to compare against the measured amplitudes.

arXiv:2608.11298 — Anomalies in Hadronic B Decays (Marianne Bouchard et al.)

This BEACH 2026 proceedings summarises SU(3)_F global fits to B→PP (P∈{π,K,η,η’}) in the topological-diagram basis, using EWP-tree relations to reduce 10 complex amplitudes to seven effective diagrams (13 real parameters). Individually the ΔS=0 (χ²/dof=1.1/2, p=58%) and ΔS=1 (1.6/2, p=45%) fits are excellent, but the combined SU(3)_F-symmetric fit collapses to χ²/dof=43/17, a 3.6σ SM discrepancy. The cause: best-fit diagram magnitudes differ across sectors by ~10×, e.g. |T̃’/T̃|=13.1±2.1, |C̃’/C̃|=8.9±1.3 — nominally 1000% SU(3)_F breaking versus the ~20–30% (f_K/f_π-1) expected. Adding η,η’ (25 parameters) worsens the fit to 4.1σ; the B→VV extension exceeds 7σ.

Imposing theory-motivated constraints makes things worse, not better: forcing |C̃/T̃|=0.2 (QCD-factorisation colour-counting) against the fitted 0.85±0.12 pushes to 4.9σ, and setting the annihilation diagram Ã=0 (expected ∼f_B/m_B-suppressed, yet fitted ∼|T̃|) gives 5.2σ. The claim to near-rigour rests on the EWP-tree relations being modified only ~10% by neglected c_7,8. This is the day’s second, independent B-anomaly hint, from the non-leptonic sector. Caveat: it is a proceedings, results drawn from Refs. [6–9]; the central assumption is exact SU(3)_F with a fixed θ_η=19.5°, and the authors themselves flag that whether a genuine ~30% breaking could accommodate the data “has to be checked” — work in progress.

arXiv:2608.12293 — Measurement of the ν̅_μ–Hydrogen CCQE cross section using the NOvA Near Detector (The NOvA Collaboration)

NOvA isolates ν̅_μH→μ⁺ⁿ from the 10.8%-hydrogen scintillator/PVC near detector (1.2×10²¹ POT), exploiting the nuclear-effect-free kinematics of a free-proton target: two BDT discriminants (topological HitID, kinematic KineID) plus data-driven control regions yield 35,509 background-subtracted signal events — the highest-statistics (anti)neutrino–hydrogen sample ever. The result, σ=0.538±0.009(stat)±0.010(syst)±0.055(flux)×10⁻³⁸ cm² at ⟨E⟩=1.9 GeV, is the most precise total QEH cross section to date, superseding the 13±6-event BNL bubble-chamber measurement. The decisive feature: the combined stat+non-flux systematic (2.5%) is more than four times below the 10.2% flux uncertainty, so the measurement can invert the usual logic and constrain the absolute ν̅_μ flux.

This lands squarely on the digest’s theme: the same cross-section systematics that were shifting DUNE sensitivities 25–30% (Puhan et al.) are precisely what a nuclear-effect-free reference process pins down. The data-correction scheme is validated by 10,000 fake-data throws showing background predictions stable against ~60% MC variations, with k_cut factors anticorrelated with the model shifts. Caveats are candidly stated: QEH purities are only ~41%/36% and signal efficiencies 3.6%/4.8%, so the analysis leans heavily on control-region-driven background subtraction; FSI weights are derived solely from neutrino-mode inclusive CC data and applied unchanged to antineutrino mode. The flux uncertainty still dominates the cross section itself — the payoff is prospective, once this becomes a flux standard candle.

item.title: Wednesday, August 12, 2026
item.description:
A muon limit amid flavor numerology

The cleanest standalone result is a number: the Fermilab g-2 collaboration sets a new direct muon EDM limit, |d_μ|<1.1×10⁻¹⁹ ecm (arXiv:2608.11124), consistent with zero. Around it the day’s bulk sits in two familiar places — neutrino/flavor model-building (a second Barger commensurate-mixing paper in as many days, plus two seesaw constructions) and QCD matter (a first Bayesian extraction of baryon susceptibilities, small-system scaling, the ultra-central flow puzzle). The collider-QI thread the memory has tracked all season reappears in a concrete tool for tau polarimetry, and a small cluster of AQN/warp-drive papers supplies the exotica.

Themes

Flavor structure, from seesaw to numerology

Barger arXiv:2608.10312 follows up his π/12 model (08-11) with a broader claim: quark and lepton mixing both collapse onto powers of a single parameter ε=|V_ub|³/10 and a π/24-quantized “digital clock” unitarity triangle, again pinning δ_CP≃296^∘ (or 244^∘) for DUNE/Hyper-K to test. He is explicit that this is parametrization-level, no dynamics. On the seesaw side, Han et al. arXiv:2608.10062 build texture-zero structures where arbitrarily large lepton-number violation coexists with sub-eV masses, predicting accessible HNLs, while Akita et al. arXiv:2608.10123 show a lepton-asymmetry mechanism that lets HNLs evade the BBN bound and enter SHiP’s reach.

QCD matter and small systems

Pihan et al. arXiv:2608.10238 report the first Bayesian extraction of baryon-number susceptibilities from RHIC BES proton cumulants, with χ_2^B tracking lattice up to μ_B∼300 MeV and a hint of enhancement beyond — notably, the nonmonotonic Ĉ_3/Ĉ_1 needs no irreducible multi-baryon correlations. Alongside, EPOS4 scaling from Pb to O (arXiv:2608.10578), ALICE’s ultra-central v_3/v_2 puzzle arXiv:2608.11199, and vorticity effects on HRG yields arXiv:2608.10561 keep the small-system/transport program that ran through last week’s OO results ticking.

Collider precision and quantum information

Beyond the muon EDM, CMS posts the first dedicated four-top resonance search in the dilepton channel arXiv:2608.10148 (SM-consistent, vector mediators excluded to 850 GeV). Haisch et al. arXiv:2608.10064 push SMEFT electroweak precision observables to NLL with the full 210-coefficient dependence — the reference basis for future e⁺e⁻ global fits, continuing the SMEFT-precision thread (Celada’s FCC-ee accounting, 08-07). And Winterbottom et al.’s TauPolaris arXiv:2608.10961 uses conditional normalizing flows to reconstruct tau polarimetric vectors, distinguishing entanglement in H→ττ at 4.3σ and improving CP sensitivity 18% — the collider-QI program moving from top tomography into a deployable analysis tool.

Speculative dark-matter astrophysics

Zhitnitsky revives the axion-quark-nugget framework twice: to explain the VASCO “mysterious transients” as ball-lightning cousins arXiv:2608.10061, and to repurpose the LHC superfluid-helium cooling system as an AQN detector arXiv:2608.10761. Paired with a warp-drive atmospheric-signature paper arXiv:2608.10800, the day’s tail is unusually speculative.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2608.11124 — New direct muon EDM limit from Fermilab g-2 tracker data; the day’s one clean number.
  • arXiv:2608.10961 — TauPolaris: normalizing-flow tau polarimetry, with a 4.3σ entanglement discrimination in H→ττ; the QI program made practical.
  • arXiv:2608.10064 — Full NLL SMEFT electroweak precision observables across all 210 Wilson coefficients; the basis future global fits will build on.
  • arXiv:2608.10312 — Barger’s commensurate quark-lepton mixing, one parameter to the 18th power; numerology, but with a falsifiable δ_CP.
  • arXiv:2608.10148 — CMS’s first dedicated four-top resonance search in the dilepton channel.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2608.10112 Calibrated correlation between heavy-quark masses and HVP observables — Beltran et al. (hep-ph) — ties m_c,m_b and their a_μ contributions to one spectral function; m_c(m_c)=1267.1(6.8) MeV.
  • arXiv:2608.10826 Muon-tagged D_s1(2460)⁺ and D_s1(2536)⁺ decays — LHCb (hep-ex) — first D_s1(2536)⁺→D_sππ branching fraction and evidence of exotic D_sπ contributions.
  • arXiv:2608.10292 ALPHA Phase I plasma haloscope — ALPHA Collaboration (hep-ex) — wire-array resonators targeting 40–80 μeV post-inflation axions near KSVZ.
  • arXiv:2608.10988 High-energy e⁻e⁺ collisions with large-angle disruptions — Zhang et al. (physics.acc-ph) — a new ε≳1 regime legacy beam-beam codes miss.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.11124 — An improved direct limit on the muon electric dipole moment (2 Collaboration et al.)

The Fermilab Muon g−2 collaboration sets d_μ⁺⁼⁽⁻⁰.35±0.19_stat±0.34_sys)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm from its 2019–20 straw-tracker data (2.34×10⁹ positrons across Run-2, Run-3a, Run-3b), yielding |d_μ|<1.10×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95% CL — a factor 1.5 improvement on the BNL E821 limit. The measurement uses the traceback method: a muon EDM tilts the spin-precession plane, producing an oscillation in the average vertical decay angle ⟨θ_y⟩ that is π/2 out of phase with the anomalous precession. Data are fit in 8 momentum bins × 2 stations × 3 runs (48 measurements, average reduced χ²⁼¹.08), combined via BLUE. Combining with BNL tightens the bound to |d_μ|<0.98(0.86)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95(90)% CL.

Why it matters: the result stays ~19 orders of magnitude above the SM prediction (∼10⁻³⁸ ecm), so it functions as a clean BSM null test on a CP-violating source independent of the anomalous-moment program, complementing the model-dependent indirect bound (1.9×10⁻²⁰).

Caveat, honestly flagged: this is systematics-limited, dominated (by far) by the vertical-alignment false-signal correction (3.12×10⁻²⁰, vs. 1.87 statistical). Notably, the analysis failed the initial soft-unblinding 3σ check, triggering the internal review that uncovered the vertical-misalignment and longitudinal-field systematics; a data-driven correction was then developed while still blinded. The alignment uncertainty is itself statistics-limited and should shrink with Runs 4–6 (2.5× the present dataset).

arXiv:2608.10961 — TauPolaris: reconstructing tau lepton polarimetric vectors with conditional normalizing flows (Daniel Winterbottom et al.)

TauPolaris estimates the undetected neutrino momenta in τ decays with a conditional normalizing flow (nine spline-coupling blocks, transformer conditioning network), modeling the full joint density p(ν|𝐜) rather than a point regression. This preserves the correlations between momentum components — crucially reconstructing the τ mass at the physical 1.78 GeV, where an MSE-trained transformer biases low and pushes the neutrino collinear with the visible τ. A gradient-ascent MAP estimate in the flow’s latent space gives per-event neutrino configurations with ~40% better angular resolution than the transformer and ~20% better than sampling. On simulated LHC pp collisions with Delphes+CMS-HPS detector modeling, three applications are demonstrated: distinguishing quantum entanglement from a classically-correlated null in H→ττ at >4.3σ (and Bell witness m_12 at 4.0σ) with 3 ab⁻¹; improving CP-violation sensitivity via ϕ_CP by 18% overall (up to 88% in 3π^±0π⁰–3π^±0π⁰, and enabling 3π^±1π⁰ reconstruction for the first time); and new polarimetric variables to suppress Z→ττ.

Why it matters: this moves the collider-QI program from top-quark tomography toward a deployable analysis tool, extending the optimal polarimetric-vector method to every τ decay topology (previously restricted to 3-prong modes with secondary vertices).

Caveats: entirely simulation-based, with hand-added track smearing to patch Delphes; the entanglement 4.3σ is an upper limit set by finite pseudoexperiments, and yields are extrapolated from a single BDT window assuming preserved S/B. The 𝒞/m_12 estimators are biased on finite data, requiring pseudoexperiment calibration.

arXiv:2608.10064 — Electroweak precision observables at NLL order in the SMEFT (Ulrich A. Haisch et al.)

Haisch and Stefanek upgrade SMEFT predictions for electroweak precision observables to next-to-leading-logarithmic accuracy by combining one-loop EW matching with two- and one-loop RG evolution from Λ to m_Z, leveraging the newly available two-loop SMEFT beta functions. A key methodological point, proven via the T-parameter contribution of the right-handed four-top operator Q_uu³³³³: two-loop matching is not needed for NLL — higher-order matching cannot generate ln(Λ/m_Z) logarithms, so one-loop matching plus NLL running suffices. The headline deliverable is numerical NLL expressions encoding the full dependence on all 210 independent Wilson coefficients (excluding only Q_H, which enters at NNLL), released as ancillary files, with explicit results tabulated for five benchmark operators.

Why it matters: whereas tree-level matching reaches only 23 operators, NLL running opens EWPO sensitivity to the entire operator set — including operators contributing only at two-loop order (Q_G, Q_HG, Q_uH³³), which have no one-loop EWPO effect at all. For the top chromomagnetic dipole Q_uG³³, the genuine two-loop L (green) terms actually dominate the L²/L (red) terms, driven by a large y_t³ beta function mixing into Q_HD. This is positioned as the reference basis for FCC-ee/CEPC global fits at sub-permille precision, continuing the SMEFT-precision thread.

Caveats: the framework is illustrated on current LEP/SLC fits and projections rather than delivering a full global result here; couplings are fixed at m_Z (differences are NNLL). The authors note complementary concurrent work (Mantani et al.; Born et al.), and stress that a complete analysis must retain both oblique and non-oblique observables.

item.title: Tuesday, August 11, 2026
item.description:
Flavor models and a quantum-gravity rerun

The day’s weight sits in the neutrino sector — a dozen-odd papers on textures, mixing predictions, oscillation systematics, and lepton-number violation. The cleanest standalone result is de Vries et al.’s arXiv:2608.07657 complete one-loop SMEFT RG analysis of neutrinoless double-beta decay, which turns operator mixing into the most stringent bounds to date on numerous dimension-seven operators. Set against that experimental-adjacent rigor, Miyauchi et al. arXiv:2608.08803 re-run the “can we see gravitons” argument that Bao et al. closed off on July 31 — the same coarse-grained-mode obstruction, now with a small opening for detector-side squeezing. Axions keep their steady uncoordinated spread, and low-energy detection hardware fills out the rest.

Themes

Neutrino flavor and oscillation observables

The load is broad but two papers stand out. Barger arXiv:2608.08394 proposes a π/12 model — trimaximal first-column mixing with charged-lepton μ–τ breaking — that pins δ=272^∘±2^∘ and predicts an ε_2 of opposite sign to the current central value, a sharp test Hyper-K resolves at 3σ. Puhan et al. arXiv:2608.08609 make the less glamorous but consequential point that DUNE’s cross-section model choice (HF-CRPA+BS over the TDR tune) shifts CP/octant sensitivity by 25–30% — systematics as decisive as the oscillation physics. Kakoti et al. arXiv:2608.07623 (modular two-zero textures), Razzaghi arXiv:2608.08179 (open-path geometric phases in layered matter), and Kar et al.’s honestly-labeled “reproducible negative result” arXiv:2608.07602 round out the model-building.

The quantum nature of gravitational waves, again

Miyauchi et al. arXiv:2608.08803 ask whether squeezing can witness a quantized GW, and reach the by-now-familiar verdict: source squeezing washes out in any realistic single-mode detector, and while a pre-squeezed detector state can produce a witness a classical field cannot, the signal is throttled by the graviton coupling. This is the second such no-go in two weeks, extending the Bao et al. arXiv:2607.27313 argument from haloscopes to gravity — the program is converging on a wall from multiple directions.

Axions from lab to lattice

Lynn arXiv:2608.07718 reports a real search: a photonic-bandgap cavity with sapphire shells reaching Q>10⁵, constraining g_aγγ over 10.25–10.45 GHz. Chen et al. arXiv:2608.08602 show small-instanton effects across KSVZ models can break the standard m_a–f_a–g_aγγ relation, opening new search regions; Masjuan arXiv:2608.08209 flags correlated large-N_c low-energy constants relevant to U(3) axion phenomenology.

Low-energy detection hardware

A cluster on pushing thresholds down: CMOS image sensors for reactor CEvNS arXiv:2608.07676, the SuperEM sub-meV architecture for the CνB and light DM arXiv:2608.08592, and table-sized spin-transparent storage rings for EDM/axion searches at JLab arXiv:2608.08551.

Deep dives

arXiv:2608.07657 — Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decays from Operator Mixing (J. de Vries et al.)

(abstract only) A complete one-loop SMEFT renormalization-group analysis shows that dimension-seven operators which do not contribute to 0νββ at tree level nonetheless generate sizable contributions via operator mixing under RG running. Accounting for the full one-loop evolution, the resulting 0νββ constraints become the most stringent bounds to date on numerous dim-7 operators — improving on limits from meson decays. The authors stress that effects beyond the first leading logarithm can dominate for specific operators and flavor combinations.

Why it matters: this is the day’s most experiment-adjacent rigor, converting the extreme sensitivity of 0νββ into a systematic constraint on the broader lepton-number-violating operator basis rather than a single-parameter mass bound. Caveat: only the abstract is available, so the numerical bounds and the flavor/operator specifics cannot be verified here.

arXiv:2608.08394 — The π/12 model: trimaximal first-column lepton mixing with charged-lepton μ–τ breaking (Vernon Barger)

Barger decomposes the first PMNS column into two independent conditions — the trimaximal norm |U_e1|²⁼²/3 (ε_1) and the μ–τ balance |U_μ1|=|U_τ1| (ε_2) — and shows that including the first JUNO result the data treat them asymmetrically: ε_1=+0.014±0.010 (consistent with zero at 1.4σ) while ε_2=+0.29⁺⁰.07_-0.13, large in central value but disfavoring zero only at 1.5σ because the profile likelihood in δ is shallow. A TM_1 neutrino sector with the electron-row condition |U_e2|/|U_e3|=2+√(3) fixes sin²θ_13=(2-√(3))/12=0.02233 and sin²θ_12=0.31811; a single charged-lepton 2–3 rotation (angle θ_e≃-1.9^∘, phase forced to α=0 by flavon alignment in an S_4×C_4×C_3×C_2 realization) generates ε_2=sin2θ_ecosα and pins δ=272^∘±2^∘, with ε_2=-0.066 — opposite in sign to the measured central value.

Why it matters: the framework is unusually falsifiable. The predicted δ sits 1.7σ from the current central value on the present profile likelihood, and Hyper-Kamiokande’s 20^∘ design precision resolves it at 3σ; a confirmed second octant (δ≈177^∘) would exclude it at >4σ. Caveat: the rigid mass sum Σm_ν=65.6 meV sits at/just beyond the DESI ΛCDM bound (64.2 meV), requiring dynamical dark energy if cosmology tightens; m_ββ=5.4 meV is below current 0νββ reach.

arXiv:2608.08803 — The Challenge of Detecting Quantum Nature of Gravitational Waves (Yu Miyauchi et al.)

Working with Gaussian states and a linear single-mode detector coupling, Miyauchi et al. use a squeezing witness W=|M|-N (W>0 certifies sub-vacuum quadrature variance impossible for any coherent-state mixture) to track whether source squeezing survives projection onto the detector-accessible wave-packet mode. Three source scenarios all fail: inflationary two-mode squeezing reduces to a thermal marginal (W_A=-N_A<0); a single-mode-squeezed stochastic background has random phases across coherence patches, washing out |M_A|; an isolated source is suppressed geometrically by W_A≤ΔΩ(ℓ_eff+1)²/8π, giving ΔΩ∼(3 km/100 Mpc)²∼10⁻⁴² for ground detectors unless emission is collimated to ℓ_eff≳10²¹.

They then show source squeezing is inessential: a pre-squeezed detector state acquires a positive witness W⁽Q)_b̃<sin²ϵ/2 from a quantized wave even when the incident mode is unexcited, whereas a classical c-number field only displaces the detector (W⁽C)_b̃=0). But the witness is throttled by the graviton–detector coupling ϵ̅=h_QG/h_th, which their strain-sensitivity table gives as ∼10⁻¹⁷–10⁻³³ across nHz–THz; detection needs ϵ≳N_trial⁻¹/4, and coherent integration (ϵ∝√(ωT)) reaches only ∼10⁻⁸.5 for a THz signal over a year.

Why it matters: this is the second no-go in two weeks, explicitly extending the Bao et al. (2607.27313) coarse-graining/weak-transfer argument to gravitational waves. The detector-squeezing loophole is real but doesn’t defeat the coupling suppression — the program’s wall is confirmed from another direction. Caveat: results are restricted to Gaussian states and linear single-mode coupling, which the authors argue is the optimistic case.
